title: Concurrent sessions cause cross-tenant KV-cache reuse, corrupting tool-call structured output
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported malformed JSON and truncated structured tool-call outputs when running concurrent function/tool invocations at scale. The corruption appears only under high concurrency where requests are routed to the same serving shard/pool and frequent prefix/KV cache operations are present. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigations, and the runtime fix to tag KV cache entries by session/tenant to prevent cross-request interleaving.

Symptoms:
- Customer-facing errors: 'Unexpected end of JSON input', 'malformed toolcall output', and occasional function invocation routing to wrong tool payload.
- Failures reproduced in Hosted (us-west1), two Dedicated pools (d-edgenet-3), and one Private deployment behind a customer proxy where autoscaling added nodes.
- Correlation with heavy streaming + function-call workloads (chat systems that call multiple helper tools in a single response).

Why it matters: Structured output and tool/function calling are core to our developer contracts. These failures caused outages for paying customers and multiple escalations to Support and Solutions. Fix is required ASAP with a staged rollout and a safe rollback plan.
reproduction_steps: 1) Seed a multi-tenant cluster (hosted or dedicated) with runtime-1.18 and ensure KV cache prefixing enabled.
2) Start 200 concurrent chat sessions that perform 3 sequential tool calls per turn and use streaming responses with short token chunks.
3) Ensure requests are routed through the same serving shard (controlled by routing policy / load balancer tweak) to increase chance of cache collision.
4) Observe occasional truncated JSON objects in the tool output stream and mismatched tool payloads returned to invoking session.
5) Capture runtime logs with request ids and kvcache keys to trace the overlap (example logs attached in investigation_notes).
investigation_notes: 2026-02-28: Initial escalations from 'AcmePayments' & 'BrightHealth' reporting structured parse failures during peak usage windows.

2026-03-01: Reproduced locally using a stress harness that simulates prefix caching + streaming tool output; observed byte-level interleaving in outgoing stream when two sessions share same cache shard.
2026-03-03: Heap dump / kv-cache inspector showed entries without a tenant/session tag. Eviction and re-write race caused a stale cache blob to be re-used by an unrelated request in same shard.

2026-03-05: Hypothesis: runtime caching layer stores 'prefix blobs' keyed by model+shard+prompt-hash but not by invocation/session-id. When concurrent streaming flushes partial fragments into the KV slot, another concurrent invocation reads the partially-written blob and emits corrupted tool JSON.

2026-03-06: Verified that disabling prefix caching eliminates the corruption in stress tests but increases per-token latency and cost. This is a viable short-term mitigation while we implement a proper fix.
2026-03-08: Private deployment on customer site showed same behavior but more sensitive due to proxy buffering — introduced additional timing windows for partial writes to be visible.

2026-03-10: Added unit tests and a fuzz harness that reproduces the interleaving; confirmed root cause is lack of session-scoped cache keys and missing atomic write semantics for partial streaming flushes.
Logs: extracted example request ids: rq_8f1a2, rq_9c2b7, shard_id: s-12; KV keys: prefix::gptx::shard12::hash(0x7b) (no session tag).
timeline: 2026-02-28: Customer Support triaged and escalated to Eng SEV. Incident bridge opened.
2026-03-01: Engineering on-call replicated issue with stress harness; created ENG-31209.
2026-03-03: Emergency mitigation: recommended disabling prefix caching for impacted customers and adding rate-limit guard rails.
2026-03-06: Short-term mitigation accepted by 2 impacted customers. Started design for longer-term fix.
2026-03-09: Code change drafted to add per-invocation tags to KV-cache keys and introduce an atomic commit marker for streaming flushes.
2026-03-11: Internal review completed; integration tests added. Preparing canary rollout to a small hosted shard.
2026-03-12: Canary began in us-west1 (s-12), monitoring OK after 6 hours. Expanding to Dedicated pool d-edgenet-3 next.
Planned rollback: if errors spike >0.5% of requests or structured parse regressions reappear, revert change and re-enable prefix-caching-disable mitigation for affected tenants.
mitigation: Immediate: advise impacted customers to temporarily disable prefix/kvcache or reduce concurrency; apply per-tenant rate limit at edge to reduce shard contention. Medium-term: canary rollout of runtime change that adds session_tag to kvcache keys and atomic commit markers. Long-term: add e2e tests in CI that do concurrency + streaming toolcall sequences across tenancy modes.
fix_plan: 1) Change KV cache key format to include tenant_id and invocation_id (runtime change).
2) Implement atomic streaming flush: write a temporary staging blob and flip a single committed flag when the blob is fully flushed so readers never see partial writes.
3) Backfill patches for Dedicated orchestration to ensure shard routing keeps tenant affinity unless explicitly relaxed.
4) Add unit/fuzz tests simulating high-concurrency streaming tool calls and enforce no cross-tenant blob reads.
5) Canary rollout (hosted -> dedicated -> private) with detailed metrics: structured-parse-error-rate, kvcache-miss-rate, latency P95, and cost per token.
6) Post-deploy monitoring and post-mortem with timeline and customer remediation steps.
Estimated work: 8 engineer-days + 2 QA-days. Target release: runtime-1.19 (canary 2026-03-12, full roll 2026-03-20).
